question: Why CHG-0034?
answer:
CHG-0034 at Birmingham Motorway 006 is a silent total failure: it reports itself as healthy while delivering nothing to drivers. Figures as of 4 September 2026.

In the detected failure episode (2 to 4 September 2026) it took 63 charging attempts and delivered zero successful sessions and zero kWh, yet reported uptime of 100 percent over that window, with no fault events and no alerts raised. The status timeline shows the pattern directly: 4,000 minutes Available and 315 minutes Preparing across 63 plug-ins, meaning drivers connected and the unit never reached charging. The small amount of Charging time recorded is the tail of a session that began before the episode and ran across midnight, not a session started inside the window. Other chargers at the same station over the same window ran at 95.75 percent delivered success on 212 attempts, so demand was there and the site was otherwise working.

It was working before. Over the full observed month (6 August to 4 September 2026) it took 439 attempts with 359 successful and 12,010.5 kWh delivered, an 81.78 percent delivered success rate. The last successful charge started at 23:41 on 1 September 2026. Detection classes this as high confidence, still ongoing, and ranks it dispatch priority 1, which orders running episodes first and then by daily loss rate.

Commercially, the observed episode carries an estimated £1,151.24 of revenue at risk at a daily rate of £383.75. If the fault continues unrepaired that extrapolates to roughly £11,512.50 a month or £140,068.75 annualised. These are prioritisation estimates, not accounting-grade lost revenue, and they assume turned-away drivers did not simply charge on a neighbouring unit, which makes them an upper bound. Note also that the absence of a fault or alert says something about the monitoring, not that the unit is healthy.

metric_definitions.preparing_minutes: Plugged in but not yet charging. A unit that cannot deliver energy accumulates this without ever reaching Charging.
metric_definitions.alert_count: no description published in the semantic layer
metric_definitions.fault_count: no description published in the semantic layer
metric_definitions.zero_kwh_sessions: Attempts that transferred no energy at all, counted across every outcome category. Wider than the zero_energy outcome label, which is one category among several: a payment failure or an aborted session can also deliver nothing.
metric_definitions.failed_sessions: no description published in the semantic layer
metric_definitions.attempted_sessions: Every plug-in, whether or not energy flowed.

assumptions: Peer comparison uses the other chargers at the same station over the same window, so demand conditions are comparable.

Headline figures cover the ACTIVE EPISODE only. full_period_context covers the whole observed month. The contrast between them is what shows the unit was working before it stopped - do not present them as the same window.

evidence.timeline_note: Counts only status changes that began inside the window shown.
evidence.outcome_note: attempts_by_outcome splits the attempts by outcome label. The zero_energy row is one of those labels, not the total that delivered nothing: use metrics.zero_kwh_sessions for that, which also counts payment failures and aborted sessions that transferred no energy.

caveats: Absence of a fault or alert is evidence about the monitoring, not evidence that the charger is healthy.

Two counts here are close but not the same: failed_sessions is every attempt that did not succeed, zero_kwh_sessions is every attempt that delivered no energy. A session can fail having delivered a little energy, so the second is the smaller number. Quote whichever you mean and name it.
